'''Damir Markota''' (born '''Damir Omerhodžić''' on December 26, 1985) is a [[Croats|Croatian]] former professional [[basketball]] player who last played for [[KK Dinamo Zagreb|Dinamo Zagreb]] in the [[Croatian Basketball League|Croatian League]]. Standing at {{height|m=2.08}}, he plays at the [[Power forward (basketball)|power forward]] position.

==Professional career==
Markota, born in [[Sarajevo]] (then [[Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina|SR Bosnia and Herzegovina]], [[Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia|SFR Yugoslavia]]), fled Bosnia during [[Bosnian War|the war]] and settled in Sweden, where he began to practice basketball. He played together with [[Maciej Lampe]] in [[Stockholm]], until moving to Croatia when he was fourteen, after being invited to play in the Croatian league. Markota signed with [[KK Cibona]], but was loaned to [[KK Zabok|Zabok]] and ''Karlovac Šanac'' until the end of 2002–03. Subsequently, he received Croatian citizenship (holding Swedish as well), declining an offer to play for the [[Sweden national basketball team|Swedish national basketball team]].

Markota was an early candidate for the [[2004 NBA draft]], but soon withdrew his name from consideration.<ref name="nba.com">{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/draft2006/profiles/DamirMarkota.html|title=Profile: Damir Markota|access-date=6 April 2010|year=2006|publisher=[[National Basketball Association|NBA]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121209034809/http://www.nba.com/draft2006/profiles/DamirMarkota.html|archive-date=9 December 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was later invited to the [[Croatia national basketball team|Croatian national team]], and in 2005 he changed his last name from "Omerhodžić" to "Markota" (his mother's maiden name).<ref name="nba.com" />

He was eventually chosen by the [[San Antonio Spurs]] in the second round of the [[2006 NBA draft]], 59th overall, then immediately traded to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]]. During the summer of 2006, the Bucks signed Markota to a multi-year contract after the Spurs traded his draft rights for the higher of the Bucks’ two [[2007 NBA draft]] second-round picks.

In February 2007, the Bucks assigned Markota to [[Tulsa 66ers]] of the [[NBA Development League]], in order to further improve his play.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20080416130325/http://mlntherawfeed.squarespace.com/basketball-transactions/2007/2/2/milwaukee-bucks-assign-rookie-forward-damir-markota-to-tulsa-66ers-of-nba-develoment-league-nba-d-league.html Milwaukee Bucks Assign Rookie Forward Damir Markota to Tulsa 66ers of NBA Development League]</ref>

On September 7, Markota was waived by the Bucks,<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20090308105259/http://www.nba.com/bucks/news/Markota_Waived_070907.html Bucks request waivers on Damir Markota]</ref> and signed with Russian team [[Spartak St. Petersburg]] on a two-year contract two days later.<ref>[http://www.bcspartak.ru/news.php?s=812 Баскетбольный клуб "Спартак" (Санкт-Петербург)]{{dead link|date=December 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} {{in lang|ru}}</ref> However, in early 2008, he switched to Lithuanian club [[BC Žalgiris|Žalgiris Kaunas]].<ref>[http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/23714/zalgiris-lands-damir-markota Zalgiris lands Damir Markota]</ref>

On August 14, 2008, Markota was signed by Cibona, returning to the team he represented as a youngster<ref>[http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/34457/180 Cibona brings back Markota]</ref> but, after a series of unsatisfying performances upon recovering form knee injury, he was suspended for clashing with the coach.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20080930013623/http://sportskenovosti.hr/index.php?cmd=show_clanak&clanak_id=4809 Bermudski trokut u Ciboni - nakon Callowaya, nestao i Markota!] {{in lang|hr}}</ref>

On October 28, 2008 [[ViveMenorca]], of the [[Asociación de Clubs de Baloncesto|Spanish ACB]], announced the signing of Markota.<ref>[http://sportskenovosti.hr/index.php?cmd=show_clanak&clanak_id=5820 Markota joins ViveMenorca] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110721102247/http://sportskenovosti.hr/index.php?cmd=show_clanak&clanak_id=5820 |date=2011-07-21 }} {{in lang|hr}}</ref><ref>[http://www.menorcabasquet.com/noticia.php?id=3167 Markota to wear #11]{{dead link|date=December 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} {{in lang|es}}</ref> In January 2009, he joined [[CB Bilbao Berri|Iurbentia Bilbao]].<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20110723190753/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/ulebcup/home/news/i/42415/448 Bilbao brings in Markota.]</ref>

On September 1, 2010, he signed a one-year deal with [[KK Union Olimpija|Union Olimpija]] in Slovenia.<ref>[https://www.talkbasket.net/2749-olimpija-add-damir-markota.html Olimpija add Damir Markota]</ref> In January 2012 he left [[KK Union Olimpija|Union Olimpija]] due to lack of payment and signed with [[KK Zagreb]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/adriatic-league/33903/damir_markota_officially_joins_kk_zagreb.html |title=Damir Markota officially joins KK Zagreb |access-date=2012-01-02 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120513070519/http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/adriatic-league/33903/damir_markota_officially_joins_kk_zagreb.html |archive-date=2012-05-13 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

He signed a contract with [[Beşiktaş men's basketball team|Beşiktaş]] in August 2012.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=10805 |title=Damir Markota signs with Beşiktaş |access-date=2012-08-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120828194718/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=10805 |archive-date=2012-08-28 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On September 27, 2013, he signed a three-month contract with [[Brose Baskets]].<ref>{{cite web|title=BROSE BASKETS adds Markota|url=http://www.euroleague.net/euroleaguenews/transactions/2013-14-signings/i/117160/8177/brose-baskets-adds-markota|publisher=Euroleague.net|access-date=27 September 2013|url-status=bot: unknown|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131202221451/http://www.euroleague.net/euroleaguenews/transactions/2013-14-signings/i/117160/8177/brose-baskets-adds-markota|archive-date=2 December 2013}}</ref> On November 25, 2013, he signed with his former club [[Bilbao Basket]] until the end of the season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Damir Markota vuelve el Bilbao Basket|url=http://www.bilbaobasket.biz/es/noticias/leer%20más/398/Damir%20Markota%20vuelve%20el%20Bilbao%20Basket.html|publisher=bilbaobasket.biz|language=es|access-date=25 November 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305035427/http://www.bilbaobasket.biz/es/noticias/leer%20m%C3%A1s/398/Damir%20Markota%20vuelve%20el%20Bilbao%20Basket.html|archive-date=5 March 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In October 2014 Markota returns to [[KK Cibona|Cibona]] for the third time signing a contract to last until the end of the season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Damir Markota u Ciboni!|url=http://www.cibona.com/2014/10/damir-markota-u-ciboni/|language=hr|publisher=KK Cibona |date=17 October 2014 }}</ref> On January 2, 2015, he parted ways with Cibona.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/croatia/147072/cibona-zagreb-officially-part-ways-with-damir-markota.html |title=Cibona Zagreb officially part ways with Damir Markota |access-date=2015-01-03 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150103043123/http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/croatia/147072/cibona-zagreb-officially-part-ways-with-damir-markota.html |archive-date=2015-01-03 |url-status=dead }}</ref> The same day he signed with Turkish team [[İstanbul Büyükşehir Belediyespor (basketball)|İstanbul BB]].<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/147094/istanbul-bsb-announces-vujacic-jenkins-and-markota.html Istanbul BSB announces Vujacic, Jenkins and Markota]</ref>

On June 17, 2017, Markota signed with Turkish club [[Uşak Sportif]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Usak Sportif signs Ian Miller, Jordan Hamilton, Isaiah Miles and Damir Markota|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/237377/usak-sportif-signs-ian-miller-jordan-hamilton-isaiah-miles-and-damir-markota.html#refresh_ce|access-date=June 17, 2017|work=Sportando.com|date=June 17, 2017}}</ref> On December 4, 2017, he parted ways with Uşak,<ref>[https://www.sportando.com/en/turkey/bsl/256236/usak-sportif-part-ways-with-damir-markota-and-mutlu-demir.html Usak Sportif part ways with Damir Markota and Mutlu Demir]</ref> and signed with Croatian club [[KK Cedevita|Cedevita]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Stiže pojačanje! Damir Markota potpisao za Cedevitu|url=https://www.kkcedevita.hr/hr/novosti/stize-pojacanje-damir-markota-pred-potpisom-za-cedevitu|access-date=4 December 2017|work=kkcedevita.hr|date=4 December 2017|language=hr|archive-date=5 December 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171205093112/https://www.kkcedevita.hr/hr/novosti/stize-pojacanje-damir-markota-pred-potpisom-za-cedevitu|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In September 2018 Markota returned to [[KK Cibona|Cibona]] for the fourth time in his career.<ref>{{cite news|title=KK Cibona signs Damir Markota|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/europe/croatia/288852/kk-cibona-signs-damir-markota.html|work=sportando.com|date=17 September 2018|access-date=18 September 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180918160537/https://sportando.basketball/en/europe/croatia/288852/kk-cibona-signs-damir-markota.html|archive-date=18 September 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In July 2019 Markota signed with the Montenegrin [[KK Mornar Bar|Mornar]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Damir Markota (ex Cibona) joins Mornar Bar|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Sweden/news/585028/Damir-Markota-(ex-Cibona)-joins-Mornar-Bar|work=eurobasket.com|date=4 July 2019}}</ref>

Markota started the 2020–21 season with the Croatian side [[KK Zabok|Zabok]] but on October 23, 2020, he signed with [[KK Cibona|Cibona]] for the fifth time in his career.<ref>{{cite news|title=SLUŽBENO: Damir Markota u Ciboni!|url=https://www.cibona.com/2020/10/sluzbeno-damir-markota-u-ciboni/|work=cibona.hr|date=23 October 2020|language=hr}}</ref> After a conflict with coach [[Vladimir Jovanović (basketball)|Vladimir Jovanović]], in April 2021, Markota left Cibona.<ref>{{cite news|title=Damir Markota više nije Cibonin igrač. Ovako se oprostio od kluba|url=https://www.index.hr/sport/clanak/markota-napustio-cibonu-evo-sto-je-rekao-na-rastanku-od-kluba/2265850.aspx|access-date=14 April 2021|work=index.hr|date=2 April 2021|language=hr}}</ref>

In February 2022, Markota signed with [[KK Dinamo|Dinamo]] of the Croatian second-tier [[First Men's Basketball League (Croatia)|Prva muška liga]].<ref>{{cite news|title=OGROMNO POJAČANJE / Bivši hrvatski reprezentativac potpisuje za Dinamo: 'Nisam ovo mogao odbiti, sinergija s Boysima je sjajna...'|url=https://net.hr/sport/kosarka/damir-markota-novi-igrac-kk-dinamo-789f045c-90f4-11ec-b47d-7ec62ca12a7c|access-date=18 February 2022|work=net.hr|date=4 March 2022|language=hr}}</ref>
==National team career==
Markota has also been a member of the senior men's [[Croatian national basketball team]]. With Croatia's senior national team, he played at the [[EuroBasket 2007]], [[EuroBasket 2011]], [[EuroBasket 2013]] and the [[2014 FIBA Basketball World Cup]].
